item.title: Apple faces another App Store antitrust fight, this time in Chile
item.description:
Apple is facing renewed pressure to open its iOS ecosystem as Chile pushes for alternative app stores and payment systems.


Chile seeks $80 million fine over Apple's iOS restrictions

On Friday, Chile's competition regulator asked the country's antitrust court to fine Apple approximately $80 million over alleged anticompetitive practices. The regulator also seeks corrective measures addressing Apple's restrictions on app distribution and in-app payments on iOS.

Reuters reports Chile's National Economic Prosecutor's Office (FNE) alleges Apple has restricted competition in both areas since at least 2019. The proposed fine is equal to 30% of sales from products and services linked to the alleged violations during the investigated period.

item.title: How to keep watching DVDs with VLC as Apple phases out Mac DVD support
item.description:
Apple has started retiring the technology behind its built-in DVD playback starting in macOS 27. Here's how you can still watch discs on a Mac with an optical drive and VLC.

VLC on Mac

For now, the change affects developers, not people watching DVDs on their Macs. Apple has removed the DVDPlayback framework from the macOS 27 SDK, so developers can no longer build apps against it with that SDK.

The framework itself remains in macOS 27, and Apple says it won't be removed until a future release. DVD Player also remains available and functional in macOS 27.

If you have movies on DVD, you don't have to wait for another macOS update to find a different way to play them. The free VLC app can open a DVD as a disc, giving you access to its movie, menus, chapters, audio tracks, and subtitles.

The 19- to 20-inch foldable iPad, known internally as J312, was previously expected to run iPadOS. Then, and now, its operating system is apparently undecided.

Apparently, iPadOS, macOS, or an entirely new platform are all still possibilities. And that's assuming it ever ships.

item.title: Apple is running macOS on an iPad, but you won't be able to
item.description:
Apple has macOS running on iPads internally, but despite the existence of the cross-platform experiment, it's far from becoming a reality for users anytime soon.


macOS on an iPad would make the tablet be even more like a notebook.

The idea of having an iPad that runs on macOS has been a dream scenario for some Mac users, but it has never officially become a reality. However, while the public isn't getting access to such a device in the foreseeable future, Apple is already experimenting with it.

Answering a listener's question on his "Power On" podcast for Bloomberg, Mark Gurman says that Apple has iPads running macOS internally. Apple apparently, and perhaps obviously, has been running it for a while already.

item.title: Image Playground is finally decent, and it's about time
item.description:
Apple's Image Playground is finally worth using, with better image generation and natural-language photo editing turning the once-limited Apple Intelligence feature into a practical creative tool.

Image Playground, generated with same

The improvements go beyond photorealistic images. Users can now edit existing photographs by describing what they want to change, while new controls make it easier to refine generated artwork.

In my testing, I used one of Image Playground's suggested prompts to add a lake to an existing image. The app followed my instructions and produced a result I liked, demonstrating how useful its editing tools can be for straightforward adjustments.

Image quality has also improved considerably since the original release, and the app has generally handled my prompts well. Apple still needs to offer more aspect ratios and creative controls, but Image Playground has become a decent alternative to ChatGPT for everyday photo editing.
